properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is elliptic's pure-JS SHA-1/SHA-2 implementation; elliptic is pulled in by create-ecdh, part of the crypto-browserify 3.12.1 shim which is a DIRECT dependency (vue.config.js maps node 'crypto' to crypto-browserify for the browser bundle). Ships in the bundle; no direct first-party call site found. Changeable by updating/removing the crypto-browserify dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @stablelib/poly1305 (^1.0.1, dep of @stablelib/chacha20poly1305) — the authenticator half of WalletConnect's session encryption: @walletconnect/crypto v1 (under @walletconnect/client ^1.8.0, a DIRECT dependency) and @walletconnect/utils v2.14 (under universal-provider-with-algorand). All six sites are the same package-lock declarations. Poly1305 as a MAC is quantum-safe; it rides on the X25519 agreement (ALG-1138d04b), which is not. No first-party call site — used inside the WalletConnect libs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The package is bcrypt-pbkdf ^1.0.0 — the OpenSSH bcrypt_pbkdf KDF used to protect PEM/SSH private keys, NOT password-storage bcrypt. Transitive devDependency: sshpk (via http-signature → request → browser-sync, a devDependency chain); it in turn pulls its own nested tweetnacl. Dev tooling only, not in the production bundle. The object name "bcrypt password hashing" is a slight mislabel; the KDF itself is a real, shipped-in-lockfile crypto dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Algorand node API tokens (algodToken/kmdToken/indexerToken, lines 11-16) hardcoded in the Vuex config store. The 64x'a' literal is algonode.cloud's documented public placeholder token for its free API tier — not a real leaked credential — but it is the credential string the app ships in source, and the identical placeholder literals also appear hardcoded in src/pages/Settings.vue:176-182.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @stablelib/x25519 1.0.3 — WalletConnect's session key agreement: dependency of @walletconnect/crypto v1 (under @walletconnect/client ^1.8.0, DIRECT dep) and of @walletconnect/utils v2.14 (under universal-provider-with-algorand ^2.8.2, DIRECT dep). Every WalletConnect relay session key is agreed with X25519, so relay traffic between this dApp and mobile wallets is harvest-now-decrypt-later material. No first-party call site; performed inside the WalletConnect libraries. Changeable only by the lib

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh 4.0.4 (elliptic-based ECDH) is a dependency of crypto-browserify 3.12.1, which is a DIRECT dependency of the app and is mapped in vue.config.js as the node 'crypto' fallback for the browser bundle (crypto: require.resolve("crypto-browserify")). So createEcdh over NIST/other curves is available to any bundled module that requires node crypto. No first-party call site found — the app's own key agreement is tweetnacl-based, not create-ecdh.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @stablelib/ed25519 1.0.3 — dependency of @walletconnect/relay-auth 1.0.4, which signs WalletConnect relay-auth JWTs with Ed25519. Transitive of the @walletconnect/client ^1.8.0 DIRECT dependency. Quantum-vulnerable signature scheme shipped in the bundle; no first-party call site — signing happens inside the WalletConnect library. Changeable only by WalletConnect; observable here. The app's own Ed25519 use (algosdk account keys) is reported separately as findings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 ships a full JS crypto stack (AES, X.509, RSA, PKCS#12, TLS). It reaches the PRODUCTION graph via unstorage → listhen (unstorage is pulled by @walletconnect/keyvaluestorage in the WalletConnect v2 stack) and the DEV graph via selfsigned → webpack-dev-server (@vue/cli-service devDep). In a browser bundle listhen's HTTPS-cert code is dead weight, but node-forge's implementations are what ships. No first-party call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @stablelib/chacha20poly1305 1.0.1 — the AEAD of WalletConnect's session encryption (@walletconnect/crypto v1 under @walletconnect/client ^1.8.0 DIRECT dep; @walletconnect/utils v2.14 under universal-provider-with-algorand). ChaCha20-Poly1305 is quantum-safe symmetric crypto, but session confidentiality ultimately rests on the X25519 agreement (ALG-1138d04b). No first-party call site; used inside the WalletConnect libraries.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl ^1.0.3 is a DIRECT dependency (package.json) and is actively used in first-party code: src/pages/vote/Question.vue:561 imports it and drives the app's encrypted-vote scheme — nacl.box.keyPair() (line 741), nacl.randomBytes (743), nacl.box (745), nacl.box.open (1841). tweetnacl provides X25519, Ed25519, XSalsa20-Poly1305, Poly1305 and SHA-512. A second nested copy ships under bcrypt-pbkdf (sshpk dev chain). The algorithm-level use sites are reported as separate findings.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: selfsigned@2.4.1 (dev: true in the lockfile) is a dependency of webpack-dev-server, part of the @vue/cli-service devDependency chain; it generates the self-signed localhost HTTPS certificate for the dev server using node-forge. Dev tooling only — not part of the production bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1's X.509 implementation. node-forge reaches the production graph via unstorage → listhen (WalletConnect v2 keyvaluestorage chain) and the dev graph via selfsigned → webpack-dev-server. In the browser bundle this is unused library surface (listhen's cert generation targets Node), but the X.509/PKI code ships with the dependency graph. No first-party call site.
